title: Numbers 0 to 9
length_note: Nine classes of 6 to 12 minutes each. There are ten numbers, so they are taught in small groups of one to three at a time, with the amount, the spoken word and the written digit introduced together. Zero gets its own class because 'nothing there' is a different idea from counting. Five-frames are introduced at 5 and used for 6 to 9, so each of those numbers is seen as 'five and some more'. After the numbers come writing the digits, counting in order, comparing amounts, and a mixed review. Every class is short and stands alone, so a session can stop after any class. Adults count cups, keys and coins; children count ducks, apples and balls. The questions and the tone are the same for both: calm, respectful and never babyish.

classes.title: One, two, three
classes.goal: Count up to 3 real things, say the number, and pick the right digit from three big choices.
topics: Counting by touching or pointing at each thing once
Adults: 1 to 3 cups, keys, coins. Children: 1 to 3 ducks, apples, balls
Seeing small amounts at a glance
The digits 1, 2, 3 shown beside the spoken words
Gentle 'how many?' questions with three big answers

classes.title: Four and five
classes.goal: Count up to 5 things and know that a full five-frame means 5.
topics: Counting 4 and 5 real things
Meeting the five-frame: a row of five boxes filled one at a time
Matching 4 and 5 to the frame, with one empty box for 4
The digits 4 and 5 with the spoken words
'How many?' with three big answers, mixing 1 to 5

classes.title: Zero: nothing there
classes.goal: Say 'zero' when there is nothing to count and know the digit 0.
topics: Zero as an empty plate, an empty cup or an empty basket
Adults: no keys in the hand. Children: no apples in the bowl
Taking things away one at a time until none are left
An empty five-frame means 0
The digit 0 shown beside the spoken word
'How many?' questions that include zero, with three big answers

classes.title: Six and seven
classes.goal: Show and recognise 6 and 7 as 'five and one more' and 'five and two more' on a five-frame.
topics: A full five-frame plus one extra for 6, plus two extra for 7
Counting real things placed in the frame
Telling 5, 6 and 7 apart by how they look in the frame
The digits 6 and 7 with the spoken words
'How many?' with three big answers, mixing 0 to 7

classes.title: Eight and nine
classes.goal: Show and recognise 8 and 9 on five-frames and say how many things are in a group of up to 9.
topics: A full five-frame plus three more for 8, plus four more for 9
Seeing 9 as 'one away from ten' with one empty box left over, using two frames side by side
Counting real things up to 9
The digits 8 and 9 with the spoken words
'How many?' with three big answers, mixing 0 to 9

classes.title: Reading and writing the digits
classes.goal: Recognise each digit from 0 to 9 and make each one by tracing, typing or pointing, in whichever way is comfortable.
topics: Telling look-alike digits apart, such as 6 and 9, or 1 and 7
Tracing each digit with a finger on the screen or on paper
Typing or tapping a digit when writing by hand is tiring or hard
Matching a digit to an amount, to a word and to a five-frame
No timers and no pressure; stop and rest at any point

classes.title: Counting in order, 0 to 9
classes.goal: Say the numbers from 0 to 9 in order and say which number comes just before or just after another.
topics: A number line of ten big steps
Counting up from 0 and counting back down from 9
What comes next? What comes before?
Filling in one missing number in a short row
Using real things laid out in a line: keys, coins, ducks, apples

classes.title: More, fewer or the same
classes.goal: Look at two groups and say which has more, which has fewer, or whether they are the same.
topics: Lining up two groups side by side to compare them
Words: more, fewer, same
Comparing two digits from 0 to 9
Zero as the smallest amount
Three big answers: this one, that one, or the same

classes.title: Putting it all together
classes.goal: Answer mixed 'how many?' questions for any amount from 0 to 9, by choosing the amount, the digit or the word.
topics: Mixed questions with real things, five-frames and digits
Matching amounts to digits and to words
Adults: cups, keys and coins in everyday scenes. Children: ducks, apples and balls in simple pictures
Gentle review of the numbers that need more practice
Looking back on what has been learned
